Snakemake for genomics

A hands-on course in two half days

Learn Snakemake by building a real ChIP-seq and DNase-seq pipeline on public HCT116 data, then read the lab’s own pipelines with confidence.

You can already write Python, R and bash. This course teaches you to tie those scripts into a pipeline that knows what to rerun, runs the same way on your laptop and on the cluster, and that someone else in the lab can pick up next year.

Set up your laptop See the schedule Start with module 0

Who this is for

Lab members who code but have never used Snakemake. You should be able to run commands in a terminal, read a short Python function and know what a BAM file is. You do not need cluster experience: day 1 runs entirely on your laptop (macOS, Linux, or Windows through WSL2), and day 2 shows how the same pipeline moves to SLURM.

We use Snakemake 8.27.1, the version the lab’s pipelines pin.

What you build

Over the two days you write RegPipe, a small pipeline for regulatory genomics. It aligns ChIP-seq and DNase-seq reads, filters them, calls peaks, builds consensus peaks and coverage tracks, measures how many reads land in peaks, and draws the MYC locus with plotgardener. Every module adds one idea to it, and you can check your work against a finished copy at four stopping points.

The finished RegPipe follows the same layout as the lab’s three production pipelines, so the last part of the course is reading those.

RegPipe (this course)
ChIP-seq and DNase-seq: align, filter, peaks, consensus, bigWigs, FRiP, a locus figure. Code

MicroCPipe
Micro-C from FASTQ to .pairs, .mcool and .hic, with a QC report. Field guide

TTpipe
TT-seq processing and analysis: STAR alignment, strand-split tracks, DESeq2. Field guide

ChromSimPipe
Cohesin loop-extrusion simulations compared with Hi-C, one GPU job per shard. Field guide

The data

The course data are real, public reads from HCT116 colorectal cancer cells: ENCODE ChIP-seq for CTCF and H3K27ac (each with its input control) and DNase-seq, two biological replicates each, plus ENCODE’s RAD21 peaks as a reference set. To keep everything laptop-sized, we kept only the reads that ENCODE’s GRCh38 alignments place in a 5 Mb window, chr8:125,000,000-130,000,000. That window holds MYC and the gene desert upstream of it, where the colorectal cancer risk enhancers sit. Every step that made the subset is in data/prepare/, and data/README.md lists each file’s source.

Two-day schedule

Each day is about four hours with breaks. The schedule has clock times and what to do if you stop early.

Day Module Time You leave with
1 0. Why Snakemake 20 min why a pipeline beats a folder of scripts
1 1. Rules 40 min your first rules, a dry run
1 2. Wildcards 45 min one rule for every sample
1 Stopping point A stopping-points/stopA/
1 Break 15 min
1 3. Config and samplesheets 45 min samples from a samplesheet, input functions
1 4. Rules that behave 50 min logs, benchmarks, threads, conda, peaks
1 Stopping point B stopping-points/stopB/
2 5. Running on a cluster 40 min profiles, SLURM, a launcher script
2 6. Structuring a pipeline 50 min rules split into files, switches, scripts
2 Stopping point C stopping-points/stopC/
2 Break 15 min
2 7. Beyond files 45 min checkpoints, scatter-gather, sentinels
2 8. Testing 35 min dry-run tests with pytest
2 Stopping point D stopping-points/stopD/ = the finished RegPipe
2 Capstone kickoff 30 min a plan for your own pipeline

How to use this site

Each lesson exists in three forms, all made from one source file:

  • The page (what you are reading now): the full text with every explanation, for working on your own or reading after the workshop.
  • The slides: the same lesson as reveal.js slides, for the instructor and for following along in the room. Find them under Also as: Slides on each lesson page. Press s for speaker notes, f for full screen.
  • The answers: every exercise links to a worked answer that explains why, not only what. The answer keys are public. Try the exercise first: most take five minutes, and the mistakes are where you learn.

If you fall behind, copy the folder of the last stopping point and carry on from there. Nobody needs to finish every exercise to follow the next module.

After the lessons, the field guide walks through the lab’s pipelines, the Snakemake-ify exercise turns a folder of shell scripts into a workflow, and the capstone is a pipeline of your own. Keep the cheat sheet open while you work (it also prints on two pages).
